issues.issue: Did the IAD err by ignoring evidence that Ms. Kharbanda did not have Parkinson's disease?
issues.applicant_position: Kharbanda did not have Parkinson's; her doctors diagnosed benign essential tremor, which the IAD ignored.
issues.respondent_position: IAD reasonably preferred the Respondent's neurologist; applicant's doctors did not directly refute the diagnosis.
issues.result_quote: In my view, the IAD acted reasonably in finding that there was no error in the diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease.

issues.issue: Did the IAD fail to weigh the applicant's cultural obligations to his parents in the H&C assessment?
issues.applicant_position: IAD did not properly weigh his cultural obligations to his parents in the H&C assessment.
issues.result_quote: I am also not persuaded that the Board erred in its assessment of the H&C factors.

issues.issue: Did the IAD fail to consider evidence that Ms. Kharbanda was unlikely to cause excessive demand on health and social services?
issues.applicant_position: IAD ignored the private care letter and made no individual assessment of likely demand or the family's ability to pay.
issues.respondent_position: Case is distinguishable from Hilewitz, where the parents had made extensive arrangements for the child's care.
issues.result_quote: On the record before me, I am simply unable to see any recognition or analysis of the type of care that the medical officer stated that she needed
